title: N.Y. General Obligations Law § 5-1103: written modification or discharge
summary: Section 5-1103 prevents specified written, signed modifications or discharges from failing merely for lack of consideration.
notes:
The provision covers an agreement, promise, or undertaking to change, modify, or discharge a contract, obligation, lease, mortgage, or other security interest described in the text. It requires a writing signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought or that party’s agent.

Place this statutory rule alongside Alaska Packers’ consideration analysis, Watkins’ treatment of a changed agreement, and UCC § 2-209. These are different sources with different conditions. Eliminating a consideration objection does not establish that a modification was free from duress or other defects.

topics.modification: The provision creates a signed-writing route around the consideration objection.
topics.consideration: Its effect is limited to the absence of consideration.
